source_refs.note: Exercise 14.1, Question 11: book page 267 (PDF 272); answer key PDF 311 (book page 306).

blocks.prompt: 11 (i) Find the direction cosines for the given vector: \(\underline{u} = -6\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
Direction cosines unit vector ke components hi hote hain: har component ko vector ki lambai se divide kar dein.
Yeh vector ke x, y, z axes ke saath angles \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) ke cosines hain.
Plan: lambai, phir divide, aur aakhir mein check ke squares ka jama 1 ho.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{u} = -6\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\cos\alpha, \cos\beta, \cos\gamma\).
Tareeqa: \(\cos\alpha = x/r\), \(\cos\beta = y/r\), \(\cos\gamma = z/r\), jahan \(r\) vector ki lambai hai.

Magnitude nikalein
\[r = \sqrt{36 + 9 + 4} = \sqrt{49} = 7\]
Kyun: Magnitude formula: components ke squares jama kar ke square root.

Har component ko \(7\) se divide karein
\[\cos\alpha = -\dfrac{6}{7}\]
\[\cos\beta = \dfrac{3}{7}\]
\[\cos\gamma = \dfrac{2}{7}\]
Kyun: Direction cosine = component / lambai. Yeh har axis ke saath bane right triangle mein adjacent / hypotenuse hai. Sign component wala hi rehta hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{36 + 9 + 4}{49} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Squares ka jama 1 aana chahiye (\(\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1\)), aur aa gaya.
blocks.final_answer:
\(-\frac{6}{7}, \frac{3}{7}, \frac{2}{7}\)
Negative \(\cos\alpha\): vector x-axis se obtuse angle banata hai.

blocks.prompt: 11 (ii) Find the direction cosines for the given vector: \(\underline{v} = 4\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - 5\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
Direction cosines unit vector ke components hi hote hain: har component ko vector ki lambai se divide kar dein.
Yeh vector ke x, y, z axes ke saath angles \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) ke cosines hain.
Plan: lambai, phir divide, aur aakhir mein check ke squares ka jama 1 ho.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{v} = 4\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - 5\underline{k}\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\cos\alpha, \cos\beta, \cos\gamma\).
Tareeqa: \(\cos\alpha = x/r\), \(\cos\beta = y/r\), \(\cos\gamma = z/r\), jahan \(r\) vector ki lambai hai.

Magnitude nikalein
\[r = \sqrt{16 + 4 + 25} = \sqrt{45}\]
\[= 3\sqrt{5}\]
Kyun: Magnitude formula: components ke squares jama kar ke square root.

Har component ko \(3\sqrt{5}\) se divide karein
\[\cos\alpha = \dfrac{4}{3\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{5}}{15}\]
\[\cos\beta = \dfrac{2}{3\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{5}}{15}\]
\[\cos\gamma = \dfrac{-5}{3\sqrt{5}} = -\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\]
Kyun: Direction cosine = component / lambai. Yeh har axis ke saath bane right triangle mein adjacent / hypotenuse hai. Sign component wala hi rehta hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{16 + 4 + 25}{45} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Squares ka jama 1 aana chahiye (\(\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1\)), aur aa gaya.
blocks.final_answer:
\(\frac{4}{3\sqrt{5}}, \frac{2}{3\sqrt{5}}, -\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\)
\(\frac{5}{\sqrt{5}} = \sqrt{5}\), is liye teesra cosine \(-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\) ban gaya.

blocks.prompt: 11 (iii) Find the direction cosines for the given vector: \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\), where \(P(9, 3, 13)\) and \(Q(11, 6, 19)\).
blocks.explanation:
Direction cosines unit vector ke components hi hote hain: har component ko vector ki lambai se divide kar dein.
Yeh vector ke x, y, z axes ke saath angles \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) ke cosines hain.
Plan: pehle vector khud banayenge, phir lambai, phir divide, aur aakhir mein check ke squares ka jama 1 ho.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\), where \(P(9, 3, 13)\) and \(Q(11, 6, 19)\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\cos\alpha, \cos\beta, \cos\gamma\).
Tareeqa: \(\cos\alpha = x/r\), \(\cos\beta = y/r\), \(\cos\gamma = z/r\), jahan \(r\) vector ki lambai hai.

Vector \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\) nikalein
\[\overrightarrow{PQ} = (11 - 9)\underline{i} + (6 - 3)\underline{j}\]
\[\quad + (19 - 13)\underline{k}\]
\[= 2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} + 6\underline{k}\]
Kyun: \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\) \(P\) se \(Q\) ki taraf hai, is liye har coordinate mein \(Q\) minus \(P\). Ulta karne se vector ulta ho jata aur saare cosines ke sign badal jate.

Magnitude nikalein
\[r = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 36} = \sqrt{49} = 7\]
Kyun: Magnitude formula: components ke squares jama kar ke square root.

Har component ko \(7\) se divide karein
\[\cos\alpha = \dfrac{2}{7}\]
\[\cos\beta = \dfrac{3}{7}\]
\[\cos\gamma = \dfrac{6}{7}\]
Kyun: Direction cosine = component / lambai. Yeh har axis ke saath bane right triangle mein adjacent / hypotenuse hai. Sign component wala hi rehta hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{4 + 9 + 36}{49} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Squares ka jama 1 aana chahiye (\(\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1\)), aur aa gaya.
blocks.final_answer:
\(\frac{2}{7}, \frac{3}{7}, \frac{6}{7}\)
Teeno positive hain, yani vector teeno axes ke saath acute angle banata hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki answer key (PDF 311) mein sirf 11 (i) aur (ii) ke jawab hain; 11 (iii) ka jawab chhoot gaya hai. Sahi jawab: \(\overrightarrow{PQ} = 2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} + 6\underline{k}\), is liye direction cosines \(\frac{2}{7}, \frac{3}{7}, \frac{6}{7}\) hain.
